title: Rational fixed point for a split solvable group on a proper scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and assume that $H$ is split solvable [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. Thus it has a finite series $H=H_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1$ of smooth connected closed subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, whose represented fppf quotients are $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$. Let $X$ be a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] and let $a:H\times_k X\to X$ be a $k$-scheme action, satisfying $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(h,a(h',x))=a(hh',x)$ as morphism identities. If $X(k)\ne\varnothing$, there exists $x\in X(k)$ fixed scheme-theoretically by $H$: for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $h\in H(A)$, $a_A(h,x_A)=x_A$, with $x_A$ the scalar extension of $x$. No perfection, infinitude or characteristic assumption on $k$ is imposed; $X$ need not be reduced or connected, and $H=1$ is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 (fixed point theorem), printed p.343. Complete algebraic scheme means proper finite-type k-scheme; fixedness is universal group-scheme fixedness, not only fixedness under H(k).

proof.text: First establish the $\mathbf G_a$ case for any proper finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ with a chosen $y\in Z(k)$. Use the coordinate model of [def-sc-gm-ga] and put $L=\operatorname{Spec}k[s]$, $U=D(s)$. The polynomial-domain node and the spectrum-stalk node make $L$ integral, with generic point $(0)$ lying in $U$, so $U$ is dense. It is finite type (one algebra generator) and hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only the ideals $0,k$. The complement of $U$ is the single rational point $o=(s)$. By the spectrum-stalk node its local ring is $k[s]_{(s)}$. For a nonzero element of $k(s)$, extracting the lowest powers of $s$ in numerator and denominator writes it $s^n p/q$ with $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $p(0)q(0)\ne0$. If $n\ge0$ this lies in $k[s]_{(s)}$; otherwise its inverse does. Thus this stalk is a valuation ring. On $U$ define $f(s)=a(s^{-1},y)$ using the additive orbit map.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to source $L$, target $Z$, open $U$, point $o$ and map $f$. Step 1 supplies the integral Noetherian source, dense open and valuation stalk; $Z$ is proper by assumption. The extension domain contains $U$ and $o$, hence is all of $L$. Obtain $F:L\to Z$ with $F(s)=a(s^{-1},y)$ on $U$, and put $z=F(o)\in Z(k)$. This is the infinity limit in Milne's proof, written in the reciprocal coordinate.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text:
On $V=\operatorname{Spec}k[u,s,(1+us)^{-1}]$ compare the morphisms $a(u,F(s))$ and $F(s/(1+us))$. The fractions are regular on $V$, so these are scheme morphisms by the affine-spectrum correspondence and principal-open localization. On $D(s)\subset V$ the action identity gives
$$a(u,F(s))=a(u,a(s^{-1},y))=a(u+s^{-1},y)=F(s/(1+us)).$$
Indeed $s/(1+us)$ is invertible there with inverse $u+s^{-1}$. The polynomial-domain node makes $k[u,s]$ a domain, and localization remains a domain: a fraction vanishes only when its numerator does. Thus $V$ is reduced by the spectrum-domain node and the definition of integral, and $D(s)$ is dense since it contains the zero prime. The target $Z$ is separated by properness. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] to conclude equality on $V$. The section $s=0$ is defined on all of $\operatorname{Spec}k[u]$, since $1+u0=1$; restricting gives $a(u,z)=z$ as morphisms $\mathbf G_a\to Z$. Evaluating on every $k$-algebra proves universal fixedness, without assuming $Z$ reduced or $k$ infinite.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text: For $\mathbf G_m$, apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-rational-fixed-point] with rank $r=1$ to any proper finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ having a rational point. It supplies a universally fixed rational point. Together with steps 1–3 this proves the assertion for each possible factor of the given split series; a specified group isomorphism transports the action and its universal fixedness by composition.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text: Induct on the length $s$ of the split series in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. The inductive assertion is existence of a universally fixed rational point for every smooth connected affine finite-type group supplied with a series of length at most $s$, acting on any proper finite-type scheme with a rational point. At length zero the group is $1$, so any chosen rational point is fixed by the unit identity. If $s>0$, put $N=H_1$. The tail is a split series of length $s-1$ for $N$, which is smooth and connected by the series hypothesis. It is affine and finite type: a closed subscheme of the affine finite-type $H$ is the spectrum of a quotient of its finitely generated coordinate algebra, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The restricted $N$-action therefore satisfies the induction hypotheses. Obtain a rational point $y\in X(k)$ universally fixed by $N$.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] to the restricted $N$-action on $X$; the group $N$ is separated because it is affine (its affine diagonal is induced by the surjection $k[N]\otimes_k k[N]\to k[N]$, $r\otimes t\mapsto rt$). The target is separated by properness. This gives a closed immersion $j:Y=X^N\hookrightarrow X$. Universal fixedness of $y$ puts it in $Y(k)$ by the representing property, so $Y(k)$ is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $Y$ is proper over $k$, hence finite type and separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No reduction of $X$ or $Y$ is taken.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text: The first quotient in the split series is a represented fppf quotient $q:H\to Q$ with kernel $N$ normal in $H$ and $Q\simeq\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-fixed-subscheme-quotient-action] to obtain $b:Q\times_kY\to Y$ with $j b(q,\mathrm{id})=a(\mathrm{id},j)$. Its hypotheses require only the given affine finite-type groups, closed normal kernel and represented quotient, and the separated finite-type target $X$. Apply steps 1–4 to this action on the proper finite-type $Y$, which has a rational point by step 6. Obtain $z\in Y(k)$ universally fixed by $Q$.

source.place: Theorem 16.51 and proof, printed p.343; additive limit at infinity expressed on the reciprocal affine chart, and induction through fixed subschemes using Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139.

proof.text:
Put $x=j(z)\in X(k)$. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $h\in H(A)$, the compatibility equation in step 7 and universal $Q$-fixedness give
$$a_A(h,x_A)=j_A(b_A(q_A(h),z_A))=j_A(z_A)=x_A.$$
This completes the induction. Only the successor's normality in its predecessor was used; no subgroup was assumed normal in all of $H$. Length zero, finite and imperfect fields, and nonreduced or disconnected $X$ are included.

Wrote the additive infinity limit on a reciprocal affine chart, reused the split-torus theorem and existing extension/equality/fixed-subscheme nodes, and made the full split-series induction explicit. One new statement-only lemma supplies the quotient action on a normal-subgroup fixed subscheme.

On V=Spec k[u,s,(1+us)^-1], reducedness, density of D(s) and separatedness from properness let lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext prove a(u,F(s))=F(s/(1+us)); restricting to s=0 gives universal fixedness, also for nonreduced Z. X^N is closed and proper by the universal-fixed-subscheme node (N affine, so separated) and closed-immersion-proper (c). The quotient action b comes from the new node, and j b(q,id)=a(id,j) gives fixedness under H. The new node is true: normality makes the G-action preserve X^N, G x_Q G is G x N, and fppf descent of morphisms (023Q) gives b. I tested N=1, N=G, empty Y and N=alpha_p.
